BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary point – the "Reviewer Efficiency Note".** The Seller's note asserts that clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". That is not correct on our record: no authority has been given by Amelia Frost on the 20% cap or the 18-month period, and nothing has been agreed on disclosure. The note is the Seller's drafting, not an instruction to us, and every clause has been reviewed below regardless of label. We should correct the record in writing so the Seller cannot later argue acquiescence.

---

## 1. Liability regime

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority | **Reject.** No authority exists. Revert to 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** 5x our position. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar (tipping) | **Reject on both amount and mechanics.** The deductible structure alone forfeits AUD 250k on every claim profile. |
| Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval | **Reject.** No approval exists. |
| "All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (12.3/13) | Default general regime | Keep categories separate; no hidden override | **Reject.** This is a catch-all that would drag Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims into the general cap/basket/18 months unless we win a specific carve-out for each. Reverse the default: limitations apply only to the claims they expressly name. |

## 2. Fundamental / Title warranties
Seller proposes capacity and title warranties sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity". This is a substantive transfer of value, not an administrative point: a defect in title to the shares would be capped at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase and time-barred after 18 months. **Reject.** Require a separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% of price cap, minimum six-year period, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier.

## 3. Exclusive remedy / non-reliance / limitations "apply to all Claims of any nature" (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
Read with 12.3/13, this would extend caps, baskets, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct – the Seller's draft contains no fraud carve-out at all. **Non-negotiable.** Insert an express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision, to the maximum extent enforceable. Also exclude the specific indemnities and Fundamental Warranties from the general limitations.

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2)
Seller relies on whole-data-room disclosure (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". **Reject.** Playbook requires specific, fair disclosure only. Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers; accept only matters disclosed in the specific disclosures with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Note the data-room cut-off (22 Sept 2026) is already six weeks stale – require a bring-down of specific disclosures at signing and Completion, with no new general disclosure.

Para 1.4 (no admission of liability or that any consent/payment/notice is required) is standard reservation language, but combined with general disclosure it would let the Seller argue every DD item was "disclosed" while admitting nothing about its consequences. It is only acceptable if general disclosure falls away.

## 5. Buyer knowledge (8.3)
Blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could have discovered from the data room or public records. Combined with the general disclosure, this effectively neutralises the warranty package: everything in the data room is both "disclosed" and "known". **Delete.** If any knowledge qualifier is to survive, it must be: actual knowledge of named Buyer persons only (no advisers, no constructive/"discoverable" knowledge); and it must never apply to title, capacity, fraud, Fundamental Warranties or the specific indemnities. Separately, any Seller "awareness" qualifiers must be tied to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.

## 6. Bluefen consent (Cl 3 / 6.3)
Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of a written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied – for a customer representing ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. **Reject.** Condition precedent must require (a) an effective, unconditional consent under clause 11.2 and (b) evidence that each 11.3 condition is satisfied, both delivered before Completion. "Satisfied on delivery" of a bare letter is not acceptable where the consent itself is conditional. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient; require all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours with a Buyer-controlled waiver right and a long-stop.

## 7. Riverlark facility (Cl 2 / 7)
Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, release "to be provided following Completion". Para 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge. On a debt-free/cash-free deal this is a direct price leakage risk and leaves security over the Company's assets after we own it. **Reject.** Require: current payout figure from Riverlark (not the Seller's approximation); direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed security releases and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release could only be considered with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval – neither is on the table.

## 8. Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
Seller says the AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. Para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and that on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not addressed. The bonuses are triggered by Completion and will be paid by the Company – i.e. by us – unless dealt with. **Push back.** Require a specific line item for AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, with a covenant that any shortfall is Seller-funded. Verify the on-cost figure ourselves.

## 9. Ironquay IP (Cl 11.1)
Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate". Para 4 confirms that under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The real exposure is not the payment but the risk that the Company does not own the Project Materials. **Push back.** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of ownership or transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, and remediation cost, while preserving the SOW3 cure (payment of outstanding fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion as a Completion deliverable). Do not accept or dispute the AUD 180,000 figure – require bank-verified evidence of payment status either way.

## 10. Export/privacy incident (DD-006; Cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Para 6: link sent to an unintended external address, ~1,240 records, access/scope/notification duty undetermined. Consistent with the playbook, we should not characterise this as a confirmed breach or assert harm or a notification obligation. But "not expected to be material" is the Seller's unsupported conclusion. **Push back.** Require: preservation of all logs and the exported file; a documented investigation with findings delivered pre-Completion; an update obligation through to Completion; a specific warranty as to the facts; and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, uncapped by the general regime, which can be sized or narrowed once the investigation concludes. No numeric claim either way at this stage.

## 11. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Para 8 confirms the disclosure does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. **Assess; do not concede.** Do not demand automatic Debt classification or a price deduction, but reserve the position: request the three contracts and renewal notices, confirm whether any amount has accrued pre-Completion (which would then fall under the working capital / debt-like items mechanism) and whether any renewal was committed outside the ordinary course after the locked-box/accounts date.

## 12. Tax / IP warranties
Seller treats these as "settled under the general regime". They are not – they remain OPEN. **Reject** the characterisation. Tax and IP warranties should sit in their own categories with separate caps and periods to be negotiated; the Seller's "all Claims" default (item 1) must not be allowed to resolve this by stealth. We do not need to assert unlimited liability; we simply need to keep the point open.

## 13. Title
Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. Para 10 concedes this is the source relied on and that no Buyer verification has occurred. The share register is a Company-maintained internal document supplied by the Seller. **Push back.** Require independent evidence: ASIC company extract, PPSR searches, confirmation of no encumbrances over the shares (including any Riverlark security over shares), Seller board/shareholder authorisations, and share certificates or a confirmed register reconciliation. Title warranty to remain Fundamental (item 2).

## 14. Other disclosure points
- **Office lease (para 7):** notification obligation only, not consent. Acceptable – but confirm the notice is given pre-Completion and make it a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (para 9):** restriction on assignment, not a change-of-control trigger. Acceptable on the face of it; verify the clause ourselves rather than rely on the Seller's reading.
- **Para 11 (reservation):** the Seller expressly says we must evaluate the facts against the full DD record. That cuts against the "Efficiency Note" and is useful to quote back.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "Efficiency Note" in writing** – nothing is cleared; no fallback authority has been given.
2. **Liability regime:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k first-dollar basket; 24-month general period; delete the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default.
3. **Fundamental/Title/Tax/IP/indemnities/covenants:** separate regimes; Fundamental = 100%, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge; Tax and IP remain open.
4. **Fraud carve-out:** express, from every cap, basket, time bar, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause – non-negotiable.
5. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only; delete general data-room/public-register disclosure; bring-down at signing and Completion.
6. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3; any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** CP requires effective consent plus evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met, pre-Completion; upgrade endeavours standard.
8. **Riverlark:** bank payout figure, repayment from Completion funds, security releases delivered at Completion.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, Seller-borne.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity to ownership/transfer failure; cure via payment and confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable; verify the AUD 180k independently.
11. **DD-006:** preserve logs, require investigation and updates, specific warranty and indemnity; no characterisation as breach, no number.
12. **Sandbar:** information request and reservation of rights; no automatic Debt treatment.
13. **Title:** independent ASIC/PPSR/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.

If helpful, I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up schedule or a cover email to Seller's counsel rejecting the Efficiency Note and setting out the Buyer's positions.
